Title: Predicting School Dropout and Simulating Educational Scenarios in Colombia Using Machine Learning
Authors: Fernandez, Mairely Narvaez and Morales Nuñez, Fernando Rafael and Serrezuela, Ruthber Rodrȷguez and Bermeo Cuenca, Daniel Felipe
Venue: 2025 IEEE VIII Congreso Internacional en Inteligencia Ambiental, Ingenieria de Software y Salud Electronica y Movil (AmITIC)
Abstract: School dropout continues to be a critical issue affecting the Colombian educational system, particularly among socioeconomically vulnerable populations. This study presents the design and implementation of an intelligent software platform that leverages Machine Learning (ML) algorithms to predict student dropout risk and simulate the impact of future educational interventions. Using historical data from national databases and local institutions, various predictive models-including decision trees, support vector machines, and artificial neural networks-were developed and evaluated. The best-performing model, based on neural networks, achieved over 85% accuracy in identifying students at high risk of dropping out. In addition to prediction, the system incorporates a simulation module that enables educational stakeholders to explore the effects of policy changes-such as increased access to subsidies, improved teacher quality, or expanded enrollment-within a controlled virtual environment. This dual approach not only supports data-driven decision-making but also enhances the equity and efficiency of educational interventions. By combining predictive analytics and scenario modeling, this research contributes a novel methodology and practical tool for addressing dropout in complex educational ecosystems. The proposed solution promotes early intervention and fosters the development of more inclusive and sustainable public policies in education.

Title: A Machine Learning Approach for Predicting the Anxiety Status Among O/L Students: A Case Study from Elpitiya Educational Zone
Authors: Umayangana, I. G. G. and Abeygunawardana, R.A.B.
Venue: 2026 6th International Conference on Advanced Research in Computing (ICARC)
Abstract: In Sri Lanka, anxiety and depression are common among youth. This study examined anxiety among $\mathrmO / \mathrmL$ students in the Elpitiya Educational Zone, aiming to identify influential factors and apply machine learning for early detection. After getting the IOBSL ethical clearance approval using the SCARED child questionnaire and a stratified cluster sampling method, data were collected from 417 students, representing a population of 7,060. The study constructed one main response variable (Anxiety), and five sub-anxiety categories are Panic Disorder, Generalized Anxiety, Social Anxiety, Separation Anxiety, and School Avoidance. Overall, $\mathbf6 1. 3 \%$ of respondents experienced some level of anxiety, 42.2 % with possible anxiety, and 19.1 % with specific anxiety. The Random Forest classifier yielded the best performance for predicting anxiety, with an accuracy of 63.33 %, an $F 1$-score of 0.6239, a recall of 0.6333, and a precision of 0.6710. For multi-label sub-anxiety classification, a Multioutput Classifier with Random Forest achieved an F1-score of 0.7186 and a Hamming loss of 0.3017. Significant factors influencing anxiety included gender, BMI, screen time, physical activity, sleep duration, parental employment, school type, and academic stress. Notably, female students, those under high academic pressure, and those from smaller schools are more prone to anxiety, while regular exercise and 5-7 hours of sleep help reduce it. The results support the importance of mental well-being through awareness and early intervention.

Title: Prediction of Depression, Anxiety and Stress Levels Using Dass-42
Authors: Srinath, K S and Kiran, K and Pranavi, S and Amrutha, M and Shenoy, P Deepa and Venugopal, K R
Venue: 2022 IEEE 7th International conference for Convergence in Technology (I2CT)
Abstract: Over the past few decades, many people are suffering from psychological health issues such as anxiety, depression, and stress. It is crucial to detect mental health condition on a timely basis and cure before it turns into a severe problem. In this paper, we analyze the performance of Machine learning (ML) algorithms to predict severity levels of depression, anxiety, and stress (DAS). Severity levels can be measured by the Depression, Anxiety, and Stress Scale (DASS) which consists of a set of questionnaires (DASS42). The intention of this research is to enhance and compare the performance of two different ML algorithms namely Support Vector Machine (SVM) and Logistic Regression (LR) based on classification accuracy with other algorithms. After parameter tuning SVM attains a classification accuracy of 97.35%, 97.49%, and 97.20% for Depression, Anxiety, and Stress. LR attains a classification accuracy of 98.15%, 98.05%, and 98.45% for Depression, Anxiety, and Stress dataset respectively. Parameter tuning is done for SVM and LR to obtain better accuracy with the best suitable parameters, and the results revealed that LR achieved better performance in terms of accuracy compared to SVM.

Title: AI-Driven Psychoeducational Analytics for Early Detection of Academic Risk in Colombian Schools
Authors: Torres, Ruth Y. Zuleta and Morillo, Dixon Salcedo and Velarde, Raúl Ramírez and Pérez, Pedro López
Abstract: This article presents the development of an academic management model integrating artificial intelligence, aimed at the early prediction of school failure risk. The study employed scientifically validated psychometric instruments, from which multi-stage databases were constructed, incorporating variables related to reading comprehension, mental health, spelling, and mathematical performance. Regression and clustering algorithms were compared with traditional linear approaches, showing a substantial enhancement in predictive performance. The proposed model is designed to support institutional data-driven decision-making and to guide timely pedagogical interventions. The findings confirm the high potential of artificial intelligence as a tool to strengthen educational inclusion, optimize academic management processes, and improve school performance in public education contexts marked by socioeconomic vulnerability. These findings lay the groundwork for scalable, ethical AI systems supporting inclusive education.

Title: Fostering Positive Childhood Behaviour and Psychological Growth through Proactive Art Education
Authors: Alsalami, Zaid and Mohammed, G. and Gabash, Ali and Al-Chalabi, Hayder and Tabaan, Ali K
Venue: 2024 International Conference on Emerging Research in Computational Science (ICERCS)
Abstract: Disruptive behaviour and conduct difficulties threaten children's development, resulting in academic impairment, special education use, high school dropout, substance misuse, and antisociality. When disruptive behaviours begin in primary school, these issues escalate, making early intervention crucial. New advancements are making instructional practices more accessible and appealing, while current ones require structural alterations to make them more acceptable to educators. Due to enhanced school procedures and technologies, this study examines proactive screening for behaviorally at-risk students. CNN-DBAM, a convolutional neural network-based disruptive behaviour analysis architecture, can analyze features and extract behavioural information from children's paintings. The convolution layer's nonlinear activation function and other efficient methods improve this model's early identification and support. According to CNN-DBAM, proactive art education boosts good behaviour and psychological growth. In the interest of early detection and intervention, this paper examines how art-based screening enhances school psychologist training. According to the author, proactive art instruction in schools may improve early screening and psychological assistance.

Title: Predicting Louisiana Public High School Dropout through Imbalanced Learning Techniques
Venue: 2019 18th IEEE International Conference On Machine Learning And Applications (ICMLA)
Abstract: This study is motivated by the magnitude of the problem of Louisiana high school dropout and its negative impacts on individual and public well-being. Our goal is to predict students who are at risk of high school dropout, by examining Louisiana administrative dataset. Due to the imbalanced nature of the dataset, imbalanced learning techniques including resampling, case weighting, and cost-sensitive learning have been applied to enhance the prediction performance on the rare class. Performance metrics used in this study are F-measure, recall and precision of the rare class. We compare the performance of several machine learning algorithms such as neural networks, decision trees and bagging trees in combination with the imbalanced learning approaches using an administrative dataset of size of 366k+ from Louisiana Department of Education. Experiments show that application of imbalanced learning methods produces good results on recall but decreases precision, whereas base classifiers without regard of imbalanced data handling gives better precision but poor recall. Overall application of imbalanced learning techniques is beneficial, yet more studies are desired to improve precision.

Title: An Approach Based on Feature Engineering and Machine Learning for the Prediction of Child Violence
Authors: Osses, Aníbal T. S. and Ricardo Fernandes, A. S.

Abstract: According to technical reports prepared by United Nations International Children’s Emergency Fund and World Health Organization, there is a high percentage of child violence occurring around the world. However, it is difficult to determine the type of violence the child is suffering, since the problem is dependent on reports of the victims and these ones could be imprecise. In this sense, decision support tools are of utmost importance for agents of social assistance programs. Thus, this paper proposes an approach based on feature engineering and machine learning to classify the violence suffered by a child. For this purpose, it was used a dataset obtained from a Chilean organization of social assistance for children. After the training and validation processes, the best machine learning models reached areas under the curve between 0.84 and 0.97, surpassing the state-of-the-art results.

Title: Explainable Ensemble Learning for Student Dropout Prediction in Conflict-Affected Educational Systems
Authors: Abas, Amna and Essgaer, Mansour and Dalla, Llahm Ben
Venue: 2026 IEEE 5th International Maghreb Meeting of the Conference on Sciences and Techniques of Automatic Control and Computer Engineering (MI-STA)
Abstract: This study investigates higher-education nonenrollment among secondary school graduates in Libya’s Fezzan region, formulated as a binary classification task distinguishing Continued Enrollment from Dropout Risk. A synthetic target variable was created using a rule-based scoring mechanism integrating risk and protective indicators. Advanced feature engineering produced composite indices—Parental Engagement, Student Commitment, Resource Availability, and Stress-Anxiety—while class imbalance was handled using SMOTE. Several feature-selection methods were evaluated, with LASSO proving most effective. Two ensemble models, Random Forest (RF) and XGBoost (XGB), were compared. Results show that XGBoost outperformed RF, achieving a higher F1-score and better capturing nonlinear relationships, while RF provided stable but lower performance. LIME-based interpretability indicated that high anxiety and reliance on academic support increased dropout risk, whereas strong resources and student commitment supported continuation. These findings highlight the importance of parental engagement, mental-health support, and socio-economic assistance to improve higher-education retention.

Title: Impact of Girls’ Education and Health on Adolescent Fertility: A Regression Analysis Using ASER and NFHS Data
Authors: Kaladevi, R. and UmaRani, V. and Kumar N, Vel Murugesh and Revathy, A.
Abstract: In India, advancing gender equality, economic growth, and societal well-being depends heavily on girls' education, early marriage, and women's health. Adolescent girls with higher levels of education are more likely to participate in the workforce, delay marriage, and have better health outcomes. However, there are serious socioeconomic issues because early school dropouts among females are frequently associated with child marriage, increased rates of adolescent pregnancies, and poor maternal health. Using information from the National Family Health Survey (NFHS) Phases I (2019-2020) and II (2019-2021) as well as the ASER 2024 report, this study investigates the effects of education, school infrastructure, literacy, and health determinants on adolescent fertility rates in India. The availability and usability of school bathrooms, rural and general female literacy rates, teenage anemia, substance use among women, and school enrollment and dropout rates for girls aged 15 to 16 are important factors. This research uses regression analysis to determine the most important factors that predict adolescent fertility (15-19 years), emphasizing the role of health and education indicators. Various regression analysis are compared using MSE, MAPE, R2 parameters. In order to improve health outcomes and socioeconomic advancement nationwide, the findings are intended to help Indian officials create focused interventions that will increase female schooling retention, advance healthcare programs, and lower adolescent pregnancies.

Title: A Novel Approach to Tackle and Predict Absenteeism of Students Using Deep Learning and Data Analytics
Authors: Agarwal, Harsh and Pandya, Kartik A and Khut, Deep and Lenka, Sushant and Karthik, Nimmagadda and Yadav, Vipul
Venue: 2022 International Conference on Edge Computing and Applications (ICECAA)
Abstract: Many pupils miss a lot of school each day along with many people in the corporate world. There are many reasons for absences, and they can come from inside and outside of the school. Motivational reasons for absenteeism include cases when a student may not want to go to class; these absences are typically voluntary and intentional. Other absences, however, are structurally based, meaning that students must skip class because of their living circumstances (such as needing to relocate frequently), and are therefore out of their control and are a result of an unavoidable circumstance. There are many different and connected reasons why students miss class. While absenteeism can frequently spike and then diminish, certain kids may fall victim to a vicious cycle of absences. The school, the absentee’s family, and the absentee themselves are frequently divided into three groups in academic literature when discussing absenteeism’s causes. When a child moves from elementary to high school, absenteeism frequently starts in the lower grades and gets worse. A teen could experience alienation in a new school and struggle to build relationships with instructors and other pupils. A student could decide not to go to school if it is too crowded or physically unsound. Bullying, an uninteresting curriculum, academic failure, and the sense of harsh behavioral sanctions are among more school-related reasons for absence. Most of these absences are mainly motivated, meaning that the student voluntarily chooses to skip class.The motive for the research is to find that the student might be absent due to which reason and what can be done to stop that using data analytics and deep learning techniques such as deep neural network and convolutional neural network.

Title: Breaking Development Traps: Synthetic Household Simulations for Poverty Alleviation in Rural West Bengal
Authors: Hazra, Soumyajit and Banerjee, Saptarshi and Karmakar, Samit
Venue: 2025 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence for Computing, Astronomy and Renewable Energy (AICARE)
Abstract: In rural India, poverty encompasses more than just low income; it also includes overlapping disadvantages in social inclusion, employment prospects, education, and health. Many households in West Bengal experience these limitations at the same time; seasonal work, landlessness, and a lack of public services all work together to create development traps that are hard to break. This study uses a simulation approach that combines synthetic household representations with public data to investigate those mechanisms. Examining the interactions between particular policy tools-MNREGA employment, access to Primary Health Centers (PHC), school-retention incentives, and social security pensions-at the household level is the goal. How much, for instance, can a family’s ability to consume be altered by a forty-day MNREGA guarantee or reduced medical costs? Which support combinations have the biggest impact on welfare over the long run? The primary welfare metric is Monthly Per-Capita Consumption Expenditure (MPCE), which is based on the Tendulkar Committee’s benchmark for rural poverty. Real purchasing power is captured by MPCE, which shows how households translate public services, transfers, and income into daily well-being. The analysis uses information from the NFHS-5, MNREGA performance statistics, Rural Health and Education Reports, and the 2023-24 Household Consumption Expenditure Survey. The model simulates the trajectories of individual households rather than just generating aggregate state figures. It makes it possible to observe how the impact of policy bundles is shaped by structural factors such as gender, caste, and land tenure. As a result, the work adds an applied, scenario-based perspective on policy design for rural development to traditional econometric studies.

Title: Analyzing Recorded Video to Evaluate How Engaged and Emotional Students Are in Remote Learning Environments
Authors: Abdellaoui, Benyoussef and Remaida, Ahmed and Sabri, Zineb and Abdellaoui, Mohammed and El Bouzekri El Idrissi, Younes and Moumen, Aniss
Venue: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Systems and Computer Vision (ISCV)
Abstract: The prevalence of distance learning has led to an increasing concern regarding the dropout rate in educational environments. However, efforts are being made to enhance the quality of learning in academic institutions by changing learning platforms and teaching methods. Many unresolved problems exist, such as increasing school dropout rates and little attention to students’ emotional state and health conditions. The proposed solution involves analyzing recorded student videos, which will provide valuable insights into student emotion and engagement and help to reduce the dropout rate. This paper proposes a new approach to assessing students’ engagement and emotional states in distance learning environments without direct interaction. This study suggests a system for analyzing student-recorded video sequences in remote learning scenarios. The proposed approach combines advanced algorithms and machine learning methods to assess students’ levels of engagement and identify their emotions. The study’s findings show how an intelligent application may be created to assist educators in evaluating the feelings and engagement of their students. For instructors, this application is a valuable resource. It gives them insightful information on the experiences of their students and helps them adjust their teaching methods accordingly.
